implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control Policy (P06) was approved 2026-08-31 and replaces the 2024 policy. Account management procedures are due 2026-11-30.

Enclave accounts are created in SYS-01 after U.S.-person verification and manager approval; 64 accounts (50 named users, 4 administrators, 2 break-glass, 8 service). Gaps: MES uses local and shared accounts; two departed users' accounts were still enabled (P07); no quarterly review.
Planned: automatic disable after 45 days of inactivity with a monthly inactive-account report, from 2026-10-31.
PLM enforces project and lifecycle roles (view, check-in, release). SYS-02 file permissions follow project groups. The provider enforces access in its services.
External sharing in SYS-02 is limited to 6 allow-listed domains. Gap: SFTP partner folders are not separated and CUI flows are not documented (see section 8).
Gap: two administrators hold all roles including logging settings. Planned: a log-administration role held by the IT Manager only.
Enclave laptop users are standard users. Gap: 24 engineers have local admin on CAD workstations; MES operators can edit NC programs.
Administrators use separate privileged accounts activated just in time with hardware security keys.
SYS-01 locks accounts after 10 failed attempts. Gap: MES local accounts have no lockout.
CUI and monitoring banner on enclave endpoints, virtual desktops, and MES terminals.
Enclave endpoints lock after 15 minutes with a pattern-hiding screen. Gap: MES terminals do not lock.
Suite and virtual desktop sessions end after 30 minutes idle and 12 hours total.
Remote access only through the virtual desktop gateway with MFA and compliant-device checks; no remote-access VPN; privileged remote commands need role activation.

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Gateway sessions use TLS through the provider's FIPS-validated modules (CRM).
No wireless on enclave VLANs. Corporate Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication and cannot route to enclave VLANs.
Mobile phones are blocked from enclave data except the authenticator app; enclave laptops are managed and encrypted.
Personal devices are blocked. Gap: enclave desktops can reach public AI chatbots and file-sharing sites; SFTP partners have no terms of use. Must be fixed before assessment (no POA&M allowed).
Website content with technical images is reviewed and released by the Contracts Manager.
Training rules are in POL-05 (approved 2026-08-31). Training procedures and curriculum due 2026-12-31.
Annual general awareness training (96% completion). Gap: no CUI handling, export release, or policy content.
Planned: insider threat indicators and reporting in the annual module, 2026-12-31.
Planned: role-based training for administrators, engineers who mark CUI, and quality staff who distribute drawings.
SYS-01, SYS-02, and SYS-03 log to a cloud log workspace. Gap: MES, DNC, and enclave firewall logs are not collected; event types never reviewed.
Cloud logs record user, time, source, and action. Gap: MES records show shared logins only.

control_name: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
implementation_statement: Planned: heartbeat alerts when a log source stops sending.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Gap: no log review. Planned: weekly review with alerts for mass download, impossible travel, and new mailbox rules, from 2026-11.

control_name: Audit Record Reduction and Report Generation
implementation_statement: The log workspace provides query and reporting; saved reports are not yet built.
All enclave systems, MES, and DNC synchronize to an authoritative time source.
Log access is limited to IT; the provider protects stored logs. Gap: all 4 administrators can change log settings.
Retention is 90 days. Planned: 1 year, to support DFARS 252.204-7012(e) preservation.
Log generation is on by default in cloud services; not configured on MES and DNC.
The 2024 self-assessment lacked evidence. A 20-control independent assessment was performed 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-07 (P07). Planned: annual full self-assessment against SP 800-171A objectives.
The 2024 POA&M was not maintained. The 2026 POA&M (P07) is reviewed monthly by the Vice President of Operations.
Planned: monthly control metrics (accounts, patching, scans, log review, training) reported to leadership from 2026-12.
Endpoint baselines are enforced through device management. Gap: VM and MES baselines undocumented; OT inventory last updated 2024.
Planned: change tickets with approval and security impact analysis for all enclave changes, from 2026-11.
Only named administrators change cloud, endpoint, and firewall configurations; MES configuration is limited to the Manufacturing Systems Engineer.
Endpoint security settings are enforced. Gap: VMs and MES are not hardened to a documented benchmark.
Endpoint and VM baselines block nonessential programs and ports. Gap: MES web administration and remote desktop open to the shop-floor VLAN.
Application allowlisting runs in audit mode; enforcement planned 2027-01-15.
Endpoints are inventoried in device management. Gap: no CMMC asset categories; OT inventory stale. Planned: one inventory with asset categories (section 9).
CUI locations are PLM, SYS-02 file storage, MES, DNC, and printed drawings. Gap: printed drawings on the shop floor were not recognized as CUI in the 2024 scope.
No contingency plan. The BIA (P05) was approved 2026-08-31; a contingency plan is due 2026-12-31.
regulatory_driver: None (business continuity; not an SP 800-171 Rev. 2 requirement)

implementation_statement: PLM database and file vault back up daily to an encrypted cloud backup vault; access limited to 2 administrators. Gap: MES and DNC servers are backed up weekly to a local disk only.
Recovery procedures will be documented in the contingency plan (2026-12-31).
Enclave users have unique identities in SYS-01. Gap: shared MES terminal logins and a shared DNC service account.
MFA is required for all privileged SYS-01 accounts (hardware keys). Gap: MES local administrator has no MFA.
MFA is required for all non-privileged SYS-01 accounts. Gap: MES operator logins have no MFA.
SYS-01 uses replay-resistant modern authentication. Gap: MES uses a legacy challenge-response protocol.
Enclave devices must be enrolled and compliant before access. Gap: MES terminals authenticate with shared passwords only.
Identifiers are never reused. Gap: no inactivity disable.
SYS-01 enforces 14 characters, banned passwords, no reuse, and temporary passwords. Gap: MES 6-character shared passwords; DNC service password stored in plain text.
Password entry is masked on enclave systems and MES.
POL-03 Incident Response Policy approved 2026-08-31 (P06).
Planned: tabletop with a DIBNet reporting drill on 2026-11-18.
EDR detects and isolates hosts. The CUI exfiltration runbook (P08) was approved 2026-08-31 and is untested; forensic retainer due 2026-10-31.
Planned: incident log in the IT ticketing system with a security category.
DoD reporting duties are defined in the P08 notification matrix. Gap: no DoD-approved medium assurance certificate; reporters not trained.
Provider CRM covers forensic support for cloud services. Planned: forensic retainer with evidence-imaging capability.
Incident response plan elements are in POL-03 and the P08 runbook.
IT maintenance is scheduled in tickets; CNC and CMM maintenance in the plant maintenance system.
Vendor tools are approved by IT. Gap: vendor diagnostic media is not scanned before connection to CNC controllers.
Vendor remote support uses a guest virtual desktop account with MFA, opened on request and watched.
Unauthorized maintenance personnel are escorted at all times.
Media handling rules, including printed drawings, are in POL-04 (approved 2026-08-31).
Digital CUI access is role based. Gap: printed drawings on the shop floor are readable by anyone, including escorted visitors.
Planned: CUI banner and distribution statement on MES print templates by 2026-11-30.
Digital media is protected. Gap: printed drawings are left at machines. Planned: cell drawing cabinets.
Gap: paper drawing copies travel with parts to outside processors in unsealed envelopes.
IT drives are wiped with certificates. Gap: printed drawings go to general recycling; CNC controller storage sent for repair is not sanitized.
Gap: uncontrolled USB drives load 6 legacy CNC machines. Planned: labeled drive inventory (2026-10-31) and DNC serial gateway (2027-01-31).
Badge access with badge groups for the engineering wing and server room.
Badges and server room keys are managed. Gap: visitor escort on the shop floor is inconsistent and the visitor log is incomplete. Must be fixed before assessment (no POA&M allowed).
Engineering printers are in the badge-restricted wing. Gap: 3 shop-floor printers sit in open aisles.
Cameras on entrances, dock, and server room; alarm monitored after hours.
Remote work uses virtual desktops. Gap: no written rules for printed CUI at home.
The five-policy set (P06) was approved 2026-08-31 with annual review.
This SSP v2.0, replacing the 2024 SSP. Updated on every significant change.
POL-05 Acceptable Use approved 2026-08-31; acknowledgments due 2026-10-31.
Segmented enclave architecture (cloud landing zone subnets; plant VLANs), described in P04.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Risk strategy and acceptance levels are in POL-01 and P01. First full risk assessment since 2024.
Background checks and U.S.-person verification before enclave access.
Gap: terminations are emailed to IT with no same-day requirement; 2 late disables found.
Gap: transfers out of engineering or quality are not reviewed for enclave access.
Risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 with NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01); annual update.
Gap: no vulnerability scanning. Planned: monthly authenticated scans of enclave VMs, endpoints, and MES from 2026-11.
The cloud provider is FedRAMP authorized at Moderate or higher with a CRM on file. Gap: outside processors receive CUI without DFARS 252.204-7012 flowdown; public AI tools used with CUI.
CNC controllers run vendor-embedded operating systems that cannot be patched. They are documented as Specialized Assets with compensating controls (section 9).
The enclave firewall separates enclave VLANs from the corporate network; cloud network security groups protect SYS-03 subnets; the SFTP gateway is in its own subnet.

control_name: Deny by Default: Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Cloud security groups deny by default. Gap: plant firewall allows any outbound from the engineering VLAN.
TLS for SYS-02 and virtual desktops, SSH for SFTP, IPsec for the site-to-site VPN.
Provider-managed keys for cloud storage. Gap: VPN pre-shared key never rotated and kept in a spreadsheet; SFTP host keys unmanaged.
FIPS-validated modules are confirmed for SYS-02, SYS-03 storage, and endpoints (CRM; OS certificates). Gap: not confirmed for the SFTP gateway VM and the plant firewall VPN.
Cloud storage and laptops are encrypted at rest. Gap: MES server and DNC share unencrypted; legacy CNC USB drives unencrypted.
Endpoints are patched monthly. Gap: VMs patched manually and MES quarterly. CNC controllers cannot be patched (SA-22).
EDR on enclave endpoints, VMs, MES, and DNC with automatic updates and real-time scanning.
EDR alerts are reviewed during business hours only. Gap: no egress or mass-download monitoring. Planned: 24x7 managed detection for the enclave by 2027-01-31.
CISA, vendor, and industrial control advisories are received and tracked in tickets.
Planned: DFARS 252.204-7012 and 252.204-7021 flowdown in outside processor purchase orders; send drawings only when needed.
The cloud provider's authorization is reviewed. Gap: SPRS and CMMC status of outside processors never checked.
